summary:
Junior Mission Orion is an interactive 3D space mission simulator designed to introduce children and young people to astronaut training and space exploration. Players customize an astronaut, build and manage colonies on the Moon and Mars, and complete missions while balancing essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy, and materials.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming space exploration concepts into an educational and interactive experience. Through construction, exploration, resource management, and problem-solving activities, players learn about the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.

The game also features Robbie, an AI-powered assistant that guides players, explains game mechanics, and answers questions. By combining interactive gameplay with educational references from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency, Junior Mission Orion aims to inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
details:
HOW THE PROJECT WORKS

Junior Mission Orion is a browser-based 3D educational simulator where players experience different aspects of astronaut training and space colony management. Players can customize their astronaut, visit a training center on Earth, and develop colonies on the Moon and Mars.

The main objective is to maintain a functional colony while completing different missions. Players must manage essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, electricity, materials, credits, and research. They also need to consider the astronaut's needs, such as hunger, energy, hygiene, social interaction, entertainment, and comfort.

The game includes construction systems, exploration activities, interactive characters, tools, and eight educational missions. These missions introduce concepts such as building habitats, installing solar panels, maintaining oxygen systems, recycling water, growing food, preparing expeditions, researching Martian soil, and expanding a colony.

Artificial Intelligence

The game features Robbie, an AI-powered assistant that helps players understand the simulator, explains its mechanics, provides guidance, and answers questions related to the game and selected space resources.

Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using:

- HTML5 for the structure of the application.

- CSS3 for the interface and visual design.

- JavaScript for game mechanics, interactions, and resource management.

- Three.js for rendering the 3D environments and objects.

- Groq as the AI service used for Robbie.

The experience also includes keyboard, touchscreen, and controller support, graphics settings, difficulty options, and automatic saving.

Scientific and Educational References

The project draws on educational and scientific resources from NASA, including Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos, DONKI, NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), RadLab, and Mars Trek. Educational resources from the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) were also considered.

These references help introduce topics related to astronomy, Mars exploration, space weather, life sciences, and space missions. Some game systems are simplified representations created for educational purposes and gameplay.

Creativity and Expected Impact

Junior Mission Orion combines a 3D simulation, resource management, exploration, missions, and an AI assistant in one learning experience. Its goal is to make space science more accessible and engaging for younger audiences while encouraging critical thinking, creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving.

Junior Mission Orion is an independent educational project and is not an official NASA product.
